text:
Colorado and Ottawa both arrive 3-1-1 in their last five, but from different angles. COL beat Toronto 6-3 on the road two days ago, a Maple Leafs team now winless in four, and is playing without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. OTT lost 3-2 at home to Washington when Cole Hutson won it in overtime, and is missing William Eklund (ankle). Tim Stützle has moved onto a line with Cozens and Zetterlund in his place, and Ridly Greig is up to 17:44 a night from 16:00.

The teams are close at five on five, with COL at 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and OTT at 52%. COL's results are ahead of its chances, though: finishing is producing 12.7 more goals than its chances usually yield. The special-teams matchup is COL's power play, at 0.78 expected goals a game, against an OTT penalty kill allowing 0.80, and OTT takes 4.7 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Scott Wedgewood (COL) is at -5.4 goals saved above expected this season, while projected starter Linus Ullmark (OTT) is at +8.2. Last season those numbers ran the other way, +23.6 for Wedgewood and -13.3 for Ullmark.

Nathan MacKinnon is our top COL name, with a 38% chance to score and an 83% chance at a point, and Corey Masisak of the Denver Post wrote that Parker Kelly's fourth line is "back to business as usual." Stützle leads OTT at 32% to score, with Drake Batherson at 30%.
